questions.q: What does a Role represent in Salesforce, per this lesson?
options: The exact same thing as a license
A field-level permission setting
A user's position in the company's reporting structure, arranged into a tree called the Role Hierarchy
A specific object a user is allowed to edit
questions.explain: A Role is a position in the org chart-like Role Hierarchy tree.

questions.q: By default, which records does a user see beyond the ones they personally own, per the Role Hierarchy?
options: No additional records -- the hierarchy has no effect on visibility
Records owned by users below them in the hierarchy
Records owned by users above them in the hierarchy
Records owned by every user in the entire org, regardless of hierarchy position
questions.explain: Visibility flows upward: a user sees their own records plus records owned by anyone below them in the hierarchy.

questions.q: Per this lesson, do two Sales Reps who report to the same manager automatically see each other's records by default?
options: Yes -- all users at the same hierarchy level always see each other's records
It depends entirely on the user's license type, not the hierarchy
No -- visibility doesn't flow sideways by default; only the manager above them sees both reps' records
Yes, but only for records created in the last 30 days
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that visibility does not flow sideways between peers at the same hierarchy level.

questions.q: Why might a VP and a Sales Rep get different totals running what looks like the same pipeline report, per this lesson?
options: The VP legitimately sees more records due to their higher position in the Role Hierarchy -- it's visibility working as designed, not a data bug
The VP's report is always technically broken
Role Hierarchy has no effect on report totals
Reports always return identical results regardless of who runs them
questions.explain: The lesson names this exact scenario as a common, non-bug explanation for differing report totals.

questions.q: How does a manual sharing rule relate to the Role Hierarchy's default upward visibility, per this lesson?
options: Sharing rules are required for a manager to see their own reports' records
Sharing rules replace the Role Hierarchy entirely in every org
Sharing rules only affect field-level security, not record visibility
A separate sharing rule is needed to extend visibility sideways or beyond what the hierarchy grants by default
questions.explain: The lesson notes that visibility beyond the default upward flow (like sideways) requires a separate sharing rule, covered in Lesson 29.
